archetype: Mono-red goblin swarm that converts a wide board into damage, with a storm sub-plan bolted on. strategic_frame.json calls it a 'storm-swarm' and deck-audit's override calls it aggro; the artifacts agree, because the swarm half is what the numbers show working — the token component assembles 60.0% at mean turn 3.184, the storm component 15.2%.
verdict: This deck functions and it converts. Mana is at target on every axis, the turn-3 land drop lands 90% of the time, and five checker-passed stacks record what the board actually does — including an arbitrarily repeatable Haze of Rage loop that needs no commander. What limits it is not volume but coverage: 13 interaction copies against a 5-6 target, spread over two of the five permanent classes, with one card (Chaos Warp) answering an enchantment or a land and nothing answering a graveyard. The deck has already paid for interaction twice over; it has bought the same answer repeatedly.

Reading all 79 entries: Chaos Warp answers any permanent, so enchantment and land ARE covered — one card deep, and randomly, since the owner reveals until a permanent replaces what you removed. engine.declared: Make goblins, then multiply one cheap spell across them — with Zada for the copies, rituals for the mana, and a storm payoff or a pump spell as the finish.

components.reading: Six single-target spells Zada copies; the audit prices the group at 36.4% of opening sevens and the target it gates assembles in 66.1% of games, mean turn 5.266. Four of the six draw a card. Ancestors' Aid draws nothing, but its second line — "Create a Treasure token" — is untargeted, so every Zada copy makes another Treasure, which is why the ramp axis counts it. Wild Ride is the one that adds nothing but power and haste.
Five early token makers, 31.2% of opening sevens, assembling in 60.0% of games at mean turn 3.184. This is the fastest thing the deck does and it is not commander-gated.

Two cards, 13.7% of opening sevens, and the target they gate assembles in 15.2% of games — 9.1% by turn 6. The corpus's own ladder starts at 31% for five copies; two is below the bottom rung. The audit flags the group `thin` and still emits no single point of failure, correctly: Grapeshot or Empty the Warrens satisfies it on its own, so no one card is load-bearing. The declaration is also short two cards — Haze of Rage and Spreading Insurrection both carry Storm, and checker-passed stack 005 runs Haze of Rage as the payoff in an arbitrarily repeatable loop.

Four rituals. The audit prices this group at 25.8% of opening sevens against the payoff group's 13.7%, so the ritual half is nearly twice as likely to show up as the half it is waiting on. `measured_rate` here is the whole target's 15.2%, the same figure the payoff component carries — the target is an AND of the two groups and the simulation measured one rate for it, not one per component.

lean_into.what: Pace for the swarm, hold the storm turn as opportunism.
lean_into.why: The token component assembles at 60.0% by mean turn 3.184 and the Zada-cantrip component at 66.1%; the storm component at 15.2%. The median game is the swarm plus a copied cantrip, and the deck should be built and mulliganed to that.

citations.quote: Separate ceiling from median: the full storm kill is the ceiling; the median game is the value engine under it — pace for the median, hold the ceiling as opportunism.

lean_into.what: The deck is built around Zada without being reliant on her — bank that.
lean_into.why: Of the five checker-passed stacks, two put Zada on the battlefield (001, 003) and three do not (002, 004 — which records her in the command zone — and 005). Of the three goldfish targets, one carries commander_gated true. And Frontline Heroism copies any spell targeting a single creature you control, so the copy effect itself has a second printing in the 99.

citations.quote: built around your commander is not reliant on it. A deck whose only payoff sits in the command zone hands three opponents one target

lean_into.what: Repoint interaction rather than adding to it.
lean_into.why: 13 copies against a 5-6 target is already double, and six separate cards convert a goblin's death or sacrifice into damage — Goblin Bombardment, Pashalik Mons, Siege-Gang Commander, Siege-Gang Lieutenant, Broadside Bombardiers and Boggart Shenanigans. The sixth copy of one effect is where a class-covering answer comes from.

citations.quote: Breadth before depth: three opponents mean every permanent type appears, so cover the classes — creature, artifact, enchantment, graveyard, land — before doubling any; catch-all removal earns its premium.

cut_candidates.why: The sixth card converting goblin deaths into damage, and the only one of the six that cannot point at a creature — its text is 'target player or planeswalker'. Three mana for a trigger the deck already has five ways to produce, one of which (Goblin Bombardment) also serves as the sac outlet.
cut_candidates.cost_of_cutting: Free, automatic reach that outlives a wrath. Two of the six fire with no mana and no activation — this and Pashalik Mons — and Pashalik Mons is a creature, so the sweeper that kills six goblins kills the trigger along with them. Boggart Shenanigans is an enchantment and would still be there to convert them into six damage.

citations.quote: Breadth before depth: three opponents mean every permanent type appears, so cover the classes — creature, artifact, enchantment, graveyard, land — before doubling any; catch-all removal earns its premium.

cut_candidates.why: One mana for an enchantment that does nothing at all until it holds five quest counters, and then grants +2/+0 with no evasion — more power onto a board the deck is already good at making wide, since the token component assembles at 60.0% by mean turn 3.184. It is not a duplicate anthem: Goblin Chieftain, Goblin Trashmaster and Rundvelt Hordemaster each read "Other Goblins you control get +1/+1", while Quest reads "creatures you control get +2/+0" — twice the power, on every creature, including the non-Goblin bodies this deck makes. The case against the slot is the dead early turns and the shape of the buff, not redundancy — a thinner case than a duplicated effect would have been, and the grade reflects it.
cut_candidates.cost_of_cutting: A one-mana enchantment that switches on faster here than five counters sounds: stack 002 (checker-passed) casts Empty the Warrens as the fourth spell of the turn, and that stack's own resolution log records a "final total: 8 tokens" — five quest triggers and more off one spell. What it then does is what stack 003 (checker-passed) does: that stack attacks with Zada and four Goblin tokens for trample damage, and Quest would add +2/+0 to every creature in that attack. It also dodges creature removal in a way the three anthem bodies do not.

cut_candidates.why: Four mana, then {3} and a tap, on a body that is summoning-sick the turn it lands — seven mana across two turns for one Goblin permanent. It is a Human Mercenary, so Goblin Warchief's haste, Goblin Chieftain's anthem, Brightstone Ritual's count and Skirk Prospector's sacrifice all read past it.
cut_candidates.cost_of_cutting: This is the painful one. It halves the tutor count, and it is the only card that puts a Goblin permanent from the library straight onto the battlefield — Goblin Lackey does it from hand, and only after connecting with a player. The corpus's point is that a tutor acts as an extra copy of every card; cutting it makes every 1-of exactly as findable as its own draw step.

citations.quote: A tutor is "essentially an additional copy of any card in our deck" (Commander Mechanic)

add_candidates.why: The only genuinely uncovered class, and therefore the first change to make: breadth before depth. One mana, exiles a card from a graveyard on entry, sacrifices to exile every opponent's graveyard — and if the table has no graveyard deck it sacrifices to draw a card instead, which is why it is the right shape here rather than Tormod's Crypt. It is the only add here that raises the measured class count.

open_questions.question: goldfish_targets.json declares the storm payoff group as Grapeshot and Empty the Warrens, but the deck holds four cards with the Storm keyword — Haze of Rage and Spreading Insurrection are omitted. Re-declare the group and re-run the simulation: does the 15.2% assembled rate survive?
open_questions.why_it_matters: 15.2% is the number that makes the storm plan look broken and it is the number every prescription about that plan would be sized against. If the true group is four cards, the component is not the thinnest one and Reiterate is a want rather than a need.

open_questions.question: Do Reiterate's three in-deck lines actually work — Mana Geyser + Reiterate, Storm-Kiln Artist + Seething Song + Reiterate, and Reiterate + Seething Song + Ruby Medallion?
open_questions.why_it_matters: All three are 'needs a stack scenario'. Stack 004 already refuted a popular combo-graph line for this deck by showing it presumed Krenko was the commander, so a popularity number is not evidence about this 99. Reiterate is not prescribed as an add here: deck-audit names it as the sole by_combo_line closer for the payoff group, but Reiterate copies a spell you already hold and so cannot satisfy an any_of group whose members are Grapeshot and Empty the Warrens. What it deepens is the ritual half, already the thicker of the two at 25.8% of opening sevens against 13.7%. If these lines resolve, that is the case for the card; the 15.2% assembled rate is not.

open_questions.question: With Roaming Throne entering as a Goblin, does Zada's copy trigger trigger a second time, and what do the second trigger's copies target?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Roaming Throne is already in the 99 and doubling the copy trigger would roughly double every cantrip's draw and every pump spell's damage. If it does not work, Roaming Throne is a four-mana 4/4 with Ward {2} in a deck whose modal mana value is 2 — still one of the two cards the protection axis counts, but a body rather than an engine piece.

open_questions.question: How do Zada and Frontline Heroism interact when one spell targets only Zada — does the Heroism token exist in time to be a legal target for Zada's copies, and in what order do the two triggers resolve?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Frontline Heroism is the deck's only second copy source, so what it is worth decides whether the protection gap is a 1-slot or a 2-slot problem.

open_questions.question: Does Witch's Mark satisfy 'targets only Zada' given its 'up to one target creature you control', and does each Zada copy repeat the 'discard a card, draw two'?
open_questions.why_it_matters: If it does, Witch's Mark is a second Crimson Wisps at double rate and the card-advantage reading is understated; if it does not, it is a two-mana filter spell in a slot the ignition component was counted for.

gaps: There is no deck_recon.json for this deck, so nothing here is grounded in what strong Zada lists actually run. Every add is argued from this deck's own axes and the in-identity pool, not from inclusion rates.

goldfish models resource development, not games — its own assumptions say 'no interaction, no removal' — so mean_bodies_by_turn (4.068 at turn 5, 5.257 at turn 6) is an upper bound on what Zada would find on board, not a forecast.
The interaction-breadth heuristic excludes counterspells by construction; the deck runs none, so the measured 2 needs no correction in either direction on that account.
Nothing in the artifacts measures how often the deck kills, only how often components assemble. Whether Moggcatcher's tutor is worth more than a class of coverage is a judgment, not a measurement.

The obsolescence index emits six entries for this deck (five distinct cards) and none is prescribed here: Contract Hero over Storm-Kiln Artist and Krenko, Baron of Tin Street over Pashalik Mons both discard the specific text those cards are played for — magecraft Treasures, and a death trigger that costs nothing. The index is format-agnostic and does not know which side of a trigger this deck is paid on.

deck-facts flags Throne of Eldraine verbatim — "Cannot pay an activated ability at all — the mana is restricted to casting SPELLS, and an activated ability is not a spell" — and the flag is real but narrow. Enumerating the audit's 64 nonland entries: 57 are monocoloured red, so Throne's four mana casts every Goblin, every ritual, every removal spell and the commander. The restriction bites on exactly seven cards — Idol of Oblivion, Roaming Throne, Ruby Medallion, Skullclamp, Sol Ring, Swiftfoot Boots and Throne itself — and on activated abilities, of which the deck has 22 with a mana cost (10 nonland, 12 land), Moggcatcher {3}, Siege-Gang Commander {1}{R}, Siege-Gang Lieutenant {2}, Pashalik Mons {3}{R} and both Equip {1} costs among them. The deck's most-used activations are not sinks at all: Krenko, Mob Boss ({T}), Goblin Bombardment (sacrifice a creature) and Idol of Oblivion's draw ({T}) each cost zero mana, and Skirk Prospector is a mana SOURCE. Throne is also one of the eight cards on card-advantage, an axis already under its floor of 10. No cut is proposed. Whether five mana for a recurring four earns a slot at modal mana value 2 is a judgment nothing in these artifacts measures.

Wild Magic Surge could not be grounded as an add and is not prescribed. It destroys target permanent an opponent controls, so it answers enchantment and land — both of which Chaos Warp already answers — and it therefore closes no axis: interaction-breadth would not move, and the interaction axis is seven copies OVER target. `strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite` licenses it only as depth, and "Depth is a meta call: copy the answer your table beats you with", which needs meta evidence this deck does not have. Its replacement clause is also strictly more generous to the opponent than Chaos Warp's — the revealed permanent is guaranteed and shares a card type. A deck_recon.json pass naming what these tables actually deploy would settle it.

Champion's Helm could not be grounded as an add and is not prescribed. The card itself is fine and the wording read holds: it costs {3}, equips for {1}, and grants hexproof rather than the shroud Lightning Greaves grants, so your own Crimson Wisps would still be able to target Zada. What it cannot clear is the decision test in the section that would license it. `strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance` is Cullen's taxonomy of options, and its rule is two halves: "His decision test: how critical is the commander to the plan, and what removal this table actually runs." Half one is answered against the add by this deck's own numbers — one of the three goldfish targets is commander_gated, and three of the five checker-passed stacks (002, 004, 005) do not put Zada on the battlefield, which is lean_into[1]. Half two is unanswerable, because there is no deck_recon.json for this deck (gaps[0]). That is the exact ground on which Wild Magic Surge was withdrawn, and the same standard has to apply to a protection slot. The section's own racing clause points the same way: "against light-interaction pods, skip the insurance, pay the tax, rebuild". Two cited targets also disagree about how large the protection gap is, and nothing in these artifacts settles which one governs a swarm deck whose commander is an accelerant rather than the kill: `strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density` asks for 5-7 protection slots, while `strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite` says "Answers to answers are a separate budget — Commander Deck Maker: 2-4 protection generic, 4-6 combo, 6-8 Voltron; counterspells do both jobs.", under which the measured 2 sits at the bottom of the generic band instead of three to five slots short. A deck_recon.json pass naming what these tables actually deploy would settle both halves at once.

findings.note: Re-ran `deck-audit goblin-storm --json` and compared all 16 measured.value fields: every one matches (mana-base 36, mana-sources 41, taplands 5, colour-sources 7, consistency 0.9, curve 2, ramp 15, card-advantage 8, creatures 27, interaction 13, interaction-breadth 2, sweepers 0, protection 2, threat-density 2, power 4, tutors 2). Readings re-derived independently from cards.json rather than trusted: 22 Mountains, 15 land / 64 nonland entries, curve 15/19/13/10/6 with exactly one card at 8+ (Blasphemous Act, cmc 9), 57 of 64 nonland entries mono-red and exactly 7 colourless (the seven named in gaps[5]). Every tapland clause in axes[2] is verbatim correct including Den of the Bugbear's backwards condition. Freshness clean: goldfish_metrics.json and mana_analysis.json both carry the current decklist sha c8c1c7dd; keep_first_seven_rate 0.791, mean_bodies 4.068/5.257 and land-drop t3 0.9 all check out; bracket-check re-run live returns floor 4 with game_changers [] , matching axes[14].

This is the probe test the charter names and the diagnosis passes it. The audit's probe note lists exactly ten cards (Crimson Wisps, Expedite, Fists of Flame, Forgotten Cave, Fountainport, Gempalm Incinerator, Idol of Oblivion, Renegade Tactics, Smoldering Crater, War Room) and the reading engages them by name, correctly separates the two cycling lands as selection, and grounds the Zada multiplication on stack 001 — whose resolution I read: 'five cards total (4 from copies + 1 from the original)' off scenario mana_available {R}. Reading 8 as a floor rather than a ceiling is the correct move, not an evasion.

All four component sizes and every rate match the audit: ignition 6 / 0.364 opener / 0.661 / mean turn 5.266; fodder 5 / 0.312 / 0.600 / 3.184; payoff 2 / 0.137 / 0.152 / 0.091 by turn 6; mana 4 / 0.258. single_points_of_failure [] matches the audit's [] and the reading explains why (either payoff card satisfies the group alone) — it does not manufacture a defect out of a named-combo half, which is the failure mode the charter warns about. One convention difference I checked and accepted: the diagnosis's `thinnest` flag is global across the flat four-component list (payoff true), where the audit marks thinnest per target (ignition and fodder are trivially thinnest of their one-component targets). The validator does not constrain the field and no reader is misled; the diagnosis separately quotes the audit's real `thin` flag, which is payoff-only.

orphans_stack [] is correct for all three: I read the scenario block of all five stacks (all checker.verdict == pass) and none of Boggart Shenanigans, Quest for the Goblin Lord or Moggcatcher appears in any board, hand, graveyard or stack. The list has a real `painful` entry (Moggcatcher) so it did not dodge the job, and the superlative in it survives enumeration — a regex for 'search your library' over all 79 entries returns only Goblin Matron (library to hand) and Moggcatcher, so 'the only card that puts a Goblin permanent from the library straight onto the battlefield' holds. Quest's cost_of_cutting quotes are verbatim: stack 002's log contains 'final total: 8 tokens' and stack 003's board is Zada plus four Goblin tokens attacking with trample (Fists of Flame grants it). The three anthems are correctly distinguished from Quest's +2/+0 to all creatures.

Soul-Guide Lantern checks out on every axis I can test. cards.csv: colourless artifact, legal_commander 'legal', so it is inside a mono-red identity. Its ETB 'exile target card from a graveyard' matches deck_audit._CLASS_PATTERNS['graveyard'] verbatim, so it genuinely raises the measured class count — and a regex for 'graveyard' over all 79 deck entries returns only self-referential text (flashback, encore, harmonize, Goblin Dark-Dwellers, Witch's Mark's Role token), confirming graveyard is the one class nothing touches. bracket_delta 4->4 is right: bracket-check re-run gives floor 4 forced by the Storm-Kiln/Haze two-card infinite, which a Lantern does not move. natural_cut Moggcatcher is consistent with cut_candidates[2]. One imprecision worth noting, not a defect: the draw mode costs '{1}, {T}, Sacrifice', and the why says 'it sacrifices to draw a card instead' without the {1}.

I initially read this as a miscount — the raw obsolescence_index.json carries 8 replacement suggestions across 7 deck cards. Running `upgrade-facts goblin-storm` reproduces the diagnosis's figure exactly: 'straight upgrades (obsolescence): 6' over five distinct deck cards (Storm-Kiln Artist, Broadside Bombardiers, Pashalik Mons, Throne of Eldraine, Idol of Oblivion). The card-level reads are also right against cards.csv: Contract Hero has no magecraft, and Krenko, Baron of Tin Street's triggers are artifact-death and a sacrifice-an-artifact activation, not Pashalik Mons's free Goblin-death trigger. The index-is-format-agnostic caveat is the correct one to draw.

The cost_of_cutting rests on a false rules claim, stated as fact with no stack behind it: 'Pashalik Mons is a creature, so the sweeper that kills six goblins kills the trigger along with them. Boggart Shenanigans is an enchantment and would still be there to convert them into six damage.' CR 603.10a (rules DB) says leaves-the-battlefield abilities look back in time, and its worked example is this exact case: an artifact with 'Whenever a creature dies, you gain 1 life' triggers twice when a spell destroys all artifacts and creatures simultaneously. Pashalik Mons's 'Whenever Pashalik Mons or another Goblin you control dies' therefore fires for every Goblin that died with it AND for itself — seven triggers under Blasphemous Act to Boggart Shenanigans's six, since Boggart triggers only on 'another Goblin'. The wrath differential is inverted, not merely overstated; the real residual value is only post-wrath deaths. This matters because the claim is the whole basis for grading the cut `contested` rather than `easy` — with it removed, Boggart Shenanigans is the cleanest cut in the document and a better natural_cut for Soul-Guide Lantern than the tutor the diagnosis itself calls painful.

ADJUDICATION, both sections fetched whole. They do genuinely conflict as written and the doc defect should be ROUTED: strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density carries Zupke's unconditioned 99-card structure ('3-5 finishers, 5-7 protection slots, 20-25 flexible strategy cards') while strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite carries an archetype-conditioned band ('Commander Deck Maker: 2-4 protection generic, 4-6 combo, 6-8 Voltron'), and nothing in either reconciles them. config.DECK_AXIS_TARGETS['protection'] hardwires the former as a universal default, which is why the audit reads UNDER. My ruling for THIS deck: the interaction-suite generic band governs, on three grounds. (1) It is the specific rule; threat-density's number is a whole-deck template quoted inside a section about conversion. (2) strategy:deckbuilding.archetype-selection — already the audit's own archetype source for this deck — independently sets combo protection at 4-6, agreeing with interaction-suite and contradicting a universal 5-7 floor; a 5-7 default asks an aggro swarm for MORE protection than the corpus asks of a combo deck, which is backwards. (3) strategy:deckbuilding.ratios closes by saying templates are 'counts of *functions*, not cards', that Hinds' own verdict is 'too one size fits all', and to 'derive the counts from the deck's actual failure modes' — and this deck's failure mode is not commander removal: the audit emits zero single_points_of_failure, 2 of 3 goldfish targets are not commander_gated, and 3 of 5 checker-passed stacks hold no Zada. Under the governing band the measured 2 sits AT the floor, which is `adequate` in this document's own usage (cf. axes[0], 36 at the top of 34-36). Grading it one of only two weaknesses in the deck overstates a 3-to-5-slot shortfall the corpus does not ask for. 'Three of the 13 cannot answer an opposing permanent at all: Impact Tremors and General Kreat hit only each opponent, Boggart Shenanigans only a player or planeswalker.' A planeswalker is a permanent. I read all 13 oracle texts from cards.json: only Impact Tremors and General Kreat can point at nothing but players, so 11 of 13 can touch an opposing permanent, not the stated 10. The companion figure is right — exactly eight can point damage at a creature (Blasphemous Act, Gempalm Incinerator, Goblin Bombardment, Goblin Negotiation, Grapeshot, Pashalik Mons, Siege-Gang Commander, Siege-Gang Lieutenant) — and the axis verdict `adequate` is unaffected. Low materiality, but it is a derived count that disagrees with the cards, and cut_candidates[0] leans on the same sentence.
